title: German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad
paragraphs: Germany's foreign and domestic intelligence services are to be given greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage after the country's parliament, the Bundestag, approved a major overhaul of its legislation.
Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, who championed the bill, has called it a "reform of the century", necessary because of the increasing threats from foreign powers.
But the Left Party's security spokeswoman, Clara Bünger, said Dobrindt was creating a new German secret police.
